correspondence.component_scope: Extreme western Talagapa opening and connection to the first mapped intermittent feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected opening is on the eastern flank/upland of Sierra Talagapa northeast of Cerro Buitrera and north of Estancia Los Guanacos. The original overview and detailed 250k image depict rugged upland contours. Farther east they depict an intermittent feeder approaching Puesto Betelo. They do not show a drainage connector across the full selected western upland interval into that feeder. Nearby printed channels to the north and south are distinct approaches and cannot be substituted for the selected connection.
correspondence.correspondence: Material pending for the extended opening-to-feeder connection. Upland setting is established; terrain association and retained model connectivity alone do not establish this entire channel interval. No hydronym is assigned to it.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: No selected headward lake or reservoir passage is depicted. The missing 100k view adds no evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Visible feeder near Betelo and Ibáñez into Cañadón Largo
correspondence.finding: The printed intermittent feeder proceeds east and southeast past Puesto Betelo, joins converging ravines near the western puestos and Puesto Ibáñez, and continues east through the valley north of Colonia Agrícola Sepaucal. The map explicitly labels the eastern valley Cañadón Largo. The selected corridor lies north of Laguna de Sepaucal and does not traverse that lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Established from the visible intermittent feeder onward at ordinary channel/valley and junction scale. The canyon/valley label is retained as such; it does not establish a whole-route river hydronym.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Intermittent channel symbols with localized vegetated valley-floor patches. Laguna de Sepaucal is a separate southern lake setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Horquetas convergence, El Fresno and Chacras de Telsen
correspondence.finding: At Las Horquetas the eastward Cañadón Largo approach joins the south-running valley drainage arriving from the north. The selected route turns south past El Fresno into Chacras de Telsen. It then receives the western Cañadón Chileno drainage in the Laguna Telsen outflow corridor and an eastern ravine at the Chacay Chico side. The continuing main valley is labeled A. Telsen. Laguna Cona and Laguna Sabalsa are neighboring northern waterbodies, outside the selected west-to-south route.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the main convergence and complete selected southward connector. No northern lake traversal or propagation of the main-river label into every feeder is inferred.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Laguna Telsen and the Sepaucal-side drainage belong to the western tributary setting, not a selected lake crossing. Local valley-floor wet/vegetated patches are shown. No reservoir or dam is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Named Telsen corridor through Telsen, Paso Moreno and the lower valley
correspondence.finding: The selected mapped channel continues southeast beside Sierra de Telsen, through the Telsen settlement and main road crossing, then through Paso Moreno and the Estancia Telsen setting. It bends south past El Paso Zapeto, Las Tres Banderas and Salto de Agua. Side ravines enter the valley, while the separately labeled Arroyo Ranquilao lies west of the selected lower route.
correspondence.correspondence: Established through the named main-river corridor, its bends and material lateral drainage settings. The lower Arroyo Telsen label supplies the provisional representative candidate, subject to the unresolved far-western opening.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: A narrowing then widening natural valley with intermittent/wet-channel and small wet-area symbols. Historical mapping does not establish present discharge or permanent water along the whole selected line. No impoundment is shown.

correspondence.component_scope: Chasicó, San Manuel and actual inland terminal in Bajo de la Tierra Colorada
correspondence.finding: South of Salto de Agua the selected channel passes Chasicó, continues southwest of Estancia San Manuel and enters an unnamed horizontally hatched shallow-water/wet depression at the northern edge of Bajo de la Tierra Colorada. The selected endpoint lies within that mapped depression. Neighboring Ranquilao and Perdido drainage and other shallow depressions occupy the wider closed-basin floor, but the selected line is not extended through them or to an ocean outlet.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at inland depression and terminal waterbody-complex scale. No precise shoreline, permanent lake level, named terminal lake, or exact river-mouth point is asserted.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Natural shallow wet/temporary-water depression in the endorheic lowland, not a reservoir. The unnamed terminal interior does not acquire the river hydronym.

correspondence.finding: The mapped river turns east north of Macclenny, receives Cedar Creek and South Prong Saint Marys River from the south, then curves northeast and north. The selected generalized route corresponds to this trunk and these junction settings. It does not follow the South Prong or Cedar Creek upstream.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_corridor_scale

correspondence.component_scope: Northward reach to Traders Hill and Folkston turn
correspondence.finding: Overlapping source views establish the northward boundary-river corridor past the tributary junctions toward Traders Hill and the broad turn east and northeast beside Folkston. The selected line follows the same river corridor at generalized scale, despite omitted meander detail. Spanish Creek and the Suwannee Canal approach from the west are distinct lateral waters, not a continuation of the selected line.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_corridor_scale

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward middle river and highway crossings
correspondence.finding: The original middle and lower maps overlap along the sinuous eastward river through the Coleraine/Flea Hill and Kings Ferry settings, onward past Clark Bluff, then through the U.S. 17 and I-95 crossing corridor. The maps distinguish Little Saint Marys River and Crooked River as separate nearby waterways; neither is used to fill the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_corridor_scale

correspondence.component_scope: Tidal lower river and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected lower route corresponds to the broad tidal Saint Marys channel past the Bells River junction and the city of Saint Marys. It ends in the mouth/entry setting of southern Cumberland Sound near Point Peter Creek, west of the ocean inlet between Cumberland and Amelia islands. North River and Bells River remain distinct estuarine branches. No selected reservoir or intervening named lake is depicted along the established downstream corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_at_corridor_scale

correspondence.component_scope: Southern opening and initial north-northwest course
correspondence.finding: The opening and long initial northward/northwestward course occupy the mapped Inland Ice east of the exposed-rock belt and east of the Tasersiaq lake setting. The ice shading, its contours and the coastal rock margin are visible throughout this opening.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_observation: No natural-river hydronym is established for the ice portion. Neither the ice contours nor the modeled line demonstrate a surface or subglacial river.

correspondence.component_scope: Short eastward return and northward middle bend
correspondence.finding: The selected short eastward turn, renewed northward course and subsequent westward bend remain in the eastern ice-margin setting. Sheet 2 covers these changes of direction and the approach to the first exposed granite/gneiss terrain north of Tasersiaq.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_observation: Tasersiaq is a separately mapped lake south of this middle bend. It is not adopted as the selected whole-route name or confused with the lower Tasersuaq lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward rock-margin crossing, northeastward return and northwestward continuation
correspondence.finding: After the westward turn, the selected corridor enters the exposed-rock belt north of Tasersiaq. Its northwestward approach, northeastward return and further northwestward continuation are covered by the mapped granite/gneiss terrain, small water bodies and narrow intervening depressions. The selected setting is not uniformly ice or one mapped continuous watercourse.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_observation: The original explains the geographic terrain throughout the modeled bends; it does not establish that the separate ice, bedrock and small-water-body intervals are one named river. Geological contacts, dykes, structural lines and elevation contours are not treated as hydrographic channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northwestward approach and westward Tasersuaq lake passage
correspondence.finding: The lower northwestern course reaches the long east-west lake corridor at the northern edge of Sheet 2. The westward selected passage lies in the southern Tasersuaq setting, labelled Taserssuaq on the older sheet. The matching lake and surrounding terrain at the southern edge of Sheet 3 establish the regional-sheet join.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_observation: Tasersuaq/Taserssuaq is retained as lake context only. It is distinct from Tasersiaq farther south and from the separate northern Tasersuaq label west of the Kangerlussuaq town-head valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward lake-to-fjord valley and material lower junction
correspondence.finding: The selected northward turn leaves the lake setting and enters the narrow sediment-filled valley shown at the lower edge of Sheet 3. That valley meets the broader east-west, sediment-filled Nivingmaneq corridor immediately before its opening into the Umiviit arm. The lake approach, sheet boundary, northern connector and receiving lower valley are all represented in the adjoining originals.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_observation: Nivingmaneq is used only as the map label locating this lower corridor. Its label placement is not treated as an independently verified river registry entry or a hydronym extending over the lake, bedrock and ice portions.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal in the Umiviit arm of Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord
correspondence.finding: The ending is at the lower sediment-filled valley where it opens into the Umiviit arm of Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord. The original shows the broad valley/deposit junction, inner marine arm and enclosing exposed-rock terrain. It is south of the town-head outlet beside Kangerlussuaq, rather than at that separate northern river mouth, and it does not end in the lower lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale.
correspondence.name_observation: Umiviit and Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord locate the receiving fjord setting. They are not accepted as a natural-river name for FID 8876.
